headline: The banks reopened on Monday with sterling close to Friday's level. Friday's weak US jobs figures and the G7's oil release are working against the dollar, while the fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis is working for it.

drivers.title: Fed rate expectations
drivers.text: After Friday's weak US jobs report, traders see little chance of a Fed rise at the 28 October meeting, though a rise in December is still priced. The minutes of the Fed's September meeting come out on Wednesday at 22:00 Dubai.

drivers.title: Oil supply
drivers.text: The G7 will release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude over four months, starting with diesel. Brent ended last week close to $100 (about £75.50) a barrel.

drivers.title: The Middle East
drivers.text: The US-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz continues. The Houthis struck an Aramco site near Riyadh on Saturday, and Saudi and Yemeni forces have begun a counteroffensive.

drivers.title: The UK side
drivers.text: The Bank of England held Bank Rate at 3.75% on 17 September, with three of the nine members voting for a rise, and its next decision is on 5 November. No major UK figures are due this week.

drivers.title: Where sterling stands
drivers.text: GBP/USD is near 1.3245. On Friday morning it fell below 1.3200, close to its lowest since June, before the US jobs figures lifted it.

lower: Fed minutes on Wednesday showing that most members want another rate rise, which would support the dollar.
The Saudi and Houthi fighting, or the standoff with Iran, cutting oil supply again, which tends to lift oil and the dollar.
A US services survey on Monday at 18:00 Dubai stronger than the 55.1 forecast, which would point to a firmer US economy.
higher: Fed minutes showing more doubt about further rises, which would add to the effect of Friday's weak jobs figures.
Oil falling further as the G7 release reaches the market, which eases US inflation worries and weakens the dollar.
A US services survey weaker than the 55.1 forecast.
watch: The US services survey (ISM) is out today at 18:00 Dubai, with 55.1 forecast against 55.4 last month, and a weaker figure would help someone selling pounds for dirhams. The Fed minutes on Wednesday at 22:00 Dubai are the week's main scheduled event.

feed.title: The banks have reopened close to Friday's level
feed.text: GBP/USD was near 1.3245 an hour after the reopening at 01:00 Dubai, against 1.3237 at Friday's close. Kraken's weekend price had dipped to about 1.3211 on Sunday morning, and that dip has been reversed. Two pieces of weekend news pull in opposite directions, set out below.

feed.title: The G7 will release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude
feed.text: G7 leaders agreed on Friday to release the oil through the International Energy Agency over four months, with a large diesel release in the first 20 days, and diesel futures fell more than 4%. More supply lowers oil prices, which eases US inflation worries and tends to weaken the dollar, so each pound buys more dirhams.

feed.title: Fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis has intensified
feed.text: The Houthis claimed a missile and drone strike on an Aramco site south of Riyadh on Saturday, and Saudi and Yemeni forces have launched a counteroffensive. Threats to oil supply tend to lift oil and the dollar, which would mean fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: US jobs report for September
feed.text: Employers added 29,000 jobs against 90,000 expected, and July and August were revised down by a combined 60,000. Unemployment rose to 4.2% against 4.1% expected, and hourly pay rose 0.1% in the month against 0.3% expected. A cooling US job market and slower pay growth make another Fed rate rise less likely; Reuters reported that US two-year yields fell 7 basis points to 4.716% and ten-year yields 6 basis points to 5.176%, and the market chance of an October rise fell to as low as 12%, so the dollar weakened and GBP/USD rose. GBP/USD jumped from 1.3205 just before 16:30 Dubai to a high of 1.3250 in the first minute and 1.3236 two minutes later, slipped to about 1.3219 by 16:33, and has since moved between about 1.3212 and 1.3241. It was near 1.3226 at 17:40 Dubai, about 0.15% above its level before the report, taking GBP/AED from about 4.850 to about 4.857.

feed.title: Oil falls back below $100 (about £76)
feed.text: Trading Economics reported on Friday that Brent fell about 3% to around $99.30 (about £75.10), as European governments considered releasing strategic oil and fuel reserves to ease fuel costs and Middle East crude flows recovered towards pre-war levels. This reverses most of Thursday's jump on the carrier report. Cheaper oil eases inflation worries and the pull of the dollar as a safe haven, which tends to help the pound against the dollar, so each pound buys slightly more dirhams. The time of the move is not known. The fall in oil came on the same day as the weaker US jobs report, and GBP/USD stood about 0.3% above Thursday evening's low near 1.3183 by 17:40 Dubai.

feed.title: Dollar eases slightly in the European morning before the US jobs report
feed.text: FXStreet reported at about 11:15 Dubai that the dollar index had slipped back below 102.00 after reaching 102.20 on Thursday, its highest since April 2025, with GBP/USD slightly above 1.3210, up about 0.2% on the day. There was no UK data this morning, and FXStreet reported that the chance of an October Fed rise priced by markets had fallen to about 24%, from over 70% a week earlier. Traders tend to trim their dollar holdings before a big US report after a strong run, which lets the pound recover a little, so each pound buys slightly more dirhams. GBP/USD rose from about 1.3205 at 07:00 Dubai to a high near 1.3218 at about 10:30 Dubai, then settled near 1.3208 by 12:30 Dubai, taking GBP/AED from about 4.850 to about 4.854 and back to about 4.851.

feed.title: Oil steadies after Thursday's jump
feed.text: The National reported on Friday that Brent eased 0.05% to $102.10 (about £77.30) and US crude 0.31% to $92.58 (about £70.10), as larger Saudi shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, 2.9 million barrels a day in September against about 1 million in August, balanced the US carrier deployment. OPEC+ meets on Sunday to set November output. Steady oil removes one source of fresh demand for the dollar, though prices above $100 (about £76) keep inflation worries and US yields high. The time of the news is not known. Oil's pause matched a quiet morning for GBP/USD, which stayed between about 1.3200 and 1.3218.

feed.title: Sterling near its lowest since June in Asian trading
feed.text: FXStreet reported GBP/USD below 1.3200 in Asian trading on Friday, near its lowest since 26 June, with the dollar index near 102, its highest since spring 2025, and traders waiting for the US jobs report. Brent rose a further 0.3% to $102.60 (about £77.70), Reuters reported. With US yields high and oil dear, money has kept flowing into the dollar, so each pound buys fewer dirhams; quiet trading before a big report tends to hold the rate near its lows. GBP/USD eased from about 1.3195 at 03:30 Dubai to a low near 1.3180 at about 05:35 Dubai, then recovered to about 1.3204 by 07:35 Dubai, taking GBP/AED from about 4.840 back to about 4.849.

feed.title: Report of a third US aircraft carrier for the Middle East lifts oil
feed.text: The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday that the US is sending the USS Theodore Roosevelt strike group to the Middle East, with up to 10,000 more troops, and a US official confirmed the deployment to The National. Brent for December settled up 4.4% at $102.31 (about £77.50) and US crude up 2.7% at $92.87 (about £70.40). Dearer oil and the risk of renewed conflict with Iran push up inflation worries and US yields and draw money into the dollar as a safe haven, so each pound buys fewer dirhams. The time of the report is not known. GBP/USD slid from about 1.3226 at 18:45 Dubai to about 1.3207 at 19:05 Dubai and to a low near 1.3183 by 19:50 Dubai, then settled near 1.3190 through the evening.

feed.title: US factory survey (ISM), September
feed.text: 54.5 against 55.0 expected and 54.6 in August, the ninth month of growth in a row. The prices paid index jumped to 77.9 from 71.1, and the employment index rose to 52.7 from 51.2. A slightly softer headline would normally weaken the dollar, but the sharp rise in prices paid points to more inflation, which keeps a Fed rise in play and supported the dollar. GBP/USD fell from 1.3234 just before the release to about 1.3221 within five minutes, then held near 1.3225 for the next half hour.

feed.title: UK 30-year borrowing costs pass 6% for the first time since 1998
feed.text: The 30-year gilt yield briefly reached about 6.03% on Thursday and the 10-year gilt yield moved above 5.50%, its highest since 2007, amid worries about energy-driven inflation, heavy government borrowing and the Budget on 28 October. The FTSE 100 lost 177.73 points. When UK yields rise because investors worry about the public finances, rather than because the economy is strong, the pound tends to fall with gilt prices, so each pound buys fewer dirhams. This weighed on sterling through Thursday alongside the firmer dollar; GBP/USD fell from about 1.3263 early on Thursday to about 1.3190 by the evening.

feed.title: US weekly jobless claims
feed.text: 197,000 new claims in the week to 26 September, against about 201,000 expected, the lowest since July. Continuing claims fell to 1.701 million. Fewer people losing their jobs points to a strong US labour market, which normally keeps a Fed rise in play and supports the dollar. GBP/USD edged up from 1.3228 just before the release to about 1.3235 within two minutes, as sterling had already fallen a long way that morning.
